description: A reverb built from eight comb filters and two allpass filters, with enough feedback on offer to make it ring on by itself

params.text: Sets the length of the reverb tail; the tooltip reads as a percentage, 0.1 seconds at 0% and 30 seconds approaching 100%, and above 100% the tail grows instead, reaching 24dB per second at 150%
A lowpass filter in the feedback path of each comb filter, sweeping from 18000Hz fully counter-clockwise down to 200Hz fully clockwise, so the tail loses its high end sooner as it is turned up
Crossfades the dry input against the reverb, dry alone fully counter-clockwise and reverb alone fully clockwise

inputs.text: The audio the reverb works on, and the dry half of what the MIX knob crossfades
Modulates the tail length, 10V covering the whole sweep of the FEEDBACK knob, and the knob and voltage are added and then clamped to the knob's own range
Modulates the damping, 10V covering the whole sweep of the DAMP knob, and the knob and voltage are added and then clamped to the knob's own range
Modulates the balance, 10V covering the whole sweep of the MIX knob, and the knob and voltage are added and then clamped to the knob's own range

outputs.text: The dry input and the reverb mixed together, clamped between -10V and 10V

notes: one channel in and one channel out; a polyphonic cable into the audio input is reduced to its first channel
with FEEDBACK above the 100% mark the reverb keeps building with nothing patched into the audio input, and a tanh saturator inside each comb filter is what stops it running away
the feedback and damping settings are recalculated once every 16 samples rather than every sample, so fast modulation of either CV input is smoothed out
